In this video, I explain which gear oil is best for Suzuki Alto VXL AGS — 75W or 90?
I also show the complete step-by-step gear oil change method, including oil capacity and how to fix AGS jerks and hard shifting.

✔ Which Oil to Use?
– Best Recommended: 75W 
– 75W-90 GL-4 is acceptable, but NOT the best
– Avoid: GL-5, 90, 140, 150 thick oils (cause hard shifting)

✔ Why 75W-80 Is Best for AGS?
– Smooth shifting
– Less jerks
– Better AGS performance
– Better cold start shifting
– Improved fuel average

✔ Gear Oil Capacity:
– 1.6 to 1.7 Liters (fill until oil comes out of the level hole)

🔧 Step-by-Step Gear Oil Change:
 1. Lift the car leveled
 2. Open the fill plug first
 3. Open the drain plug and drain completely
 4. Tighten drain plug
 5. Fill 75W-80 GL-4 oil until it overflows
 6. Close fill plug
 7. Start the car and test AGS (D, R, Manual mode)

If your Suzuki Alto has an AC coil (evaporator) leakage issue, here are the possible causes and solutions:

Causes of Coil Leakage:
 Moisture and Corrosion: Over time, moisture buildup can cause corrosion in the evaporator coil, leading to leakage.
 Physical Damage: Any impact or mishandling during maintenance can cause small cracks or punctures in the coil.
 Dirt and Debris: Accumulated dirt can lead to corrosion, weakening the coil structure.
 Manufacturing Defect: In some cases, factory defects may cause premature leakage.
 Refrigerant Leaks: If the system runs with low refrigerant for too long, it can lead to internal coil damage.

Solution: Suzuki Alto Evaporator Replacement
 Diagnose the Leak
Use a refrigerant leak detector or UV dye method to confirm the evaporator is leaking.
 Recover Refrigerant
Before replacing the evaporator, the AC system must be discharged properly.
 Remove Dashboard and AC Components
Since the evaporator is located inside the dashboard, it requires careful dismantling of panels, AC ducts, and other interior parts.
 Replace the Evaporator Coil
Install a new coil, ensuring proper fitting and connection of pipes.
 Reassemble and Recharge AC System
After reinstallation, vacuum the system to remove air and moisture, then refill it with the correct amount of refrigerant.
 Test the System
Check for any leaks and ensure proper cooling performance.
